description.fun: Porygon is made entirely of programming code, the first Pokémon ever created by computer. It doesn't need to eat or breathe, can turn itself into data to travel through cyberspace, and is copy-protected so it can't be duplicated. Satoshi Tajiri said it was a bit of irony: told he was too late for the Game Boy and should make 3D games, he put a Pokémon made of polygons into a sprite game.
description.guide: A pink and blue, polygonal Normal Pokémon, the first artificial Pokémon, made entirely of programming code. It evolves into Porygon2 when traded holding an Up-Grade. Its only major anime role was in an episode that was banned after its flashing effects sent hundreds of viewers in Japan to hospital.
description.tagline: A Pokémon built from code and polygons

description.fun: Porygon2 is Porygon upgraded with cutting-edge technology so it could work in space, though since it can't fly, it struggles in zero gravity. It learns things nobody taught it, sometimes doing things that aren't in its programming, and it talks to other Porygon2 in a language only they understand. It's the only Pokémon with a numeral in its name.
description.guide: The evolution of Porygon, introduced in Generation 2, a rounder, red and blue Normal Pokémon upgraded to work in space. It evolves from Porygon when traded holding an Up-Grade, and into Porygon-Z when traded holding a Dubious Disc. It can learn on its own.

description.fun: Porygon-Z came from extra software meant to let Porygon2 travel through alien dimensions. It didn't work: the result twitches and behaves erratically, and the experiment is generally seen as a failure, blamed on a botched update. Academics still disagree on whether it's a true evolution at all, and the 'Dubious Disc' that creates it hints that Silph Co. never approved the upgrade.
description.guide: The final form of Porygon, a Normal Pokémon introduced in Generation 4 with a head that floats apart from its body. It evolves from Porygon2 when traded holding a Dubious Disc. Its unstable behaviour suggests a computer virus or a faulty software patch.
description.tagline: An upgrade that went a bit wrong

note.text: Porygon is the only Pokémon that evolves by trading twice, with no leveling up at either step, so a Porygon-Z can be level 1.
